clue.text: Artist made less entertaining twice

indicators.note: entertaining in its sense of holding or harbouring, so one piece takes the other in

parts.note: to cut something is to make it less, reduce it
bis is Latin for twice, the call for an encore

explanation.surface: A painter has twice managed to make something duller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made less entertaining' reads as one phrase meaning duller, but splits after 'less'; bis is the call for an encore.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cubist is a painter of the early twentieth-century movement led by Picasso and Braque.

clue.text: Scarlet and black rock around ravine

indicators.note: around means the first word encloses the other

parts.note: coal is a black rock
a chine is a deep narrow ravine, a word used on the south coast of England

explanation.surface: Red and black stones lie around a deep gully.
explanation.walkthrough: A chine, on the Isle of Wight and Dorset coast of England, is a steep narrow ravine running to the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Cochineal is a scarlet dye made from crushed insects, and the colour it gives.

clue.text: Giraffe, say, one fuelling round river

indicators.note: round means one piece encircles the other

parts.note: a bowser is a tanker that refuels aircraft or vehicles

explanation.surface: A giraffe acts like a tanker refuelling around a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts R inside BOWSER. 'Giraffe, say' is a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A giraffe feeds by browsing leaves from trees, so it is an example of a leaf-eating animal.

clue.text: He painted the north of Scotland

definitions.meaning: Graham ... was a twentieth-century English painter
a former county in the far north of Scotland

explanation.definitionFit: Graham Sutherland was a British painter, and Sutherland is a historic county at the top of Scotland.

clue.text: Once a week, new head introduced party of girls

indicators.note: the word's first letter is swapped out for a different initial letter

parts.note: sennight is an archaic word for a week (seven nights), so 'Once' flags an old term

explanation.surface: Weekly, a new boss is brought in at some gathering of women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new head introduced' replaces the S at the front of SENNIGHT with H. 'Once' here means formerly, not one time.
explanation.definitionFit: A hen night is a British celebration held for a bride-to-be by her female friends before the wedding.

clue.text: Badly need swallowed fat to be completely absorbed

indicators.note: swallowed means one piece takes the other inside
badly means the letters are put together wrongly

parts.note: gross means fat, overweight

explanation.surface: A badly needy person ate fat until quite consumed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badly' rearranges NEED into ENED before the fat goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Engrossed means wholly absorbed in something, unable to look away.

clue.text: Service abolished? That's fate

parts.note: abolished means there is no more of it
RN, the Royal Navy, is one of the armed services

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the Navy has been scrapped, and calls it destiny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service abolished' reads as 'no RN'. That's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norns were the three goddesses of fate in Norse myth, so a Norn is a figure of fate.

clue.text: Forbidding expert to betray disgust

parts.note: grim means stern and forbidding
an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: A stern specialist lets slip his revulsion.
explanation.definitionFit: To grimace is to twist the face, showing distaste or disgust.

clue.text: Perfunctory fine a number received

indicators.note: received means taking the other piece in

parts.note: ten is a number
OK means fine, all right

explanation.surface: A token fine was taken by a member of the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perfunctory fine' reads as a small penalty, but the definition is 'Perfunctory' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A token gesture is a perfunctory one, done for form's sake only.

clue.text: Pious claptrap in short section of poem

indicators.note: short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a canto is a division of a long poem

explanation.surface: Sanctimonious rubbish turns up in a brief passage of verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' takes the last O from CANTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Cant is hypocritical, sanctimonious talk, insincere moralising.

clue.text: From small country, black bird goes to big landmass, calling

indicators.note: calling means spoken out, so the words are said rather than written

parts.words: black bird goes to big landmass
parts.note: a crow is a black bird and Asia the largest continent, so the phrase gives crow followed by Asia

explanation.surface: A black bird flies off from a small land to a huge continent, cawing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'calling' turns CROW + ASIA, said together, into the sound of the country's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Croatia is a small Balkan nation on the Adriatic coast.

clue.text: Old actor goes to pull on back-cloth

indicators.note: back means the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a rag is a piece of cloth
to rick is to wrench or strain, as in pulling a muscle

explanation.surface: A veteran performer goes to haul on the painted backdrop of a stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back-cloth' looks like the theatre backdrop but splits, 'back' reversing the cloth word. David Garrick was the great eighteenth-century English actor.
explanation.definitionFit: David Garrick was the leading English stage actor of the eighteenth century, so long dead.

clue.text: At work, pins notice for perusal

indicators.note: at work means set going, operating on the letters so they rearrange

explanation.surface: In the office, someone pins up a notice for people to read.
explanation.definitionFit: Perusal is close reading or examination, which is what an inspection is.

clue.text: Fine fabric in green

definitions.meaning: a fine linen or cotton cloth
a stretch of mown grass, as a bowling green

explanation.definitionFit: Lawn is both a sheer linen cloth and a mown grassy area like a green.

clue.text: What anglers cast into southern river with cold determination

indicators.note: into means the piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the Tees is a river in north-east England
anglers cast their fishing lines

explanation.surface: Fishermen cast into a river in the south with icy resolve.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tees is a river in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Steeliness is hard, cold resolve, like the hardness of steel.

clue.text: Wild West lawman needs to carry silencer

parts.note: Wyatt Earp was a famous marshal of the American frontier
to lug is to carry something heavy

explanation.surface: A frontier marshal needs to bring along a gun's silencer.
explanation.definitionFit: An earplug blocks out sound, so it is a silencer for the wearer.

clue.text: Cease, to be interested: by what flower does to seed?

definitions.meaning: stop being keen on something with age
a plant in bloom develops from a seed

explanation.walkthrough: Ignore the OCR punctuation: the first reading is 'cease to be interested by'. The second is a cryptic picture of a plant emerging from its seed.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose interest in something as one matures is idiomatically to outgrow it, and a plant literally develops from a seed.

clue.text: Dogs foul streets

indicators.note: foul means fouled up, messed, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Dogs leave mess on the town streets.
explanation.definitionFit: Setters are breeds of gundog, such as the Irish setter.

clue.text: I would see finally through thin illumination

indicators.note: through means passing inside the other piece

parts.note: slight means thin, slender
I'd is short for I would

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: I'd be able to see at last through dim light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes E from 'see'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidelight is a lamp or window giving light, so a source of illumination.

clue.text: Sign from heaven to engage long battle

indicators.note: engage in the sense of interlock or hold, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: Leo is a sign of the zodiac, written in the stars
to long or yearn for something is to pant for it

explanation.surface: A heavenly omen is enough to commit a lengthy war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sign from heaven' suggests an omen but is a star sign of the zodiac.
explanation.definitionFit: Lepanto was the 1571 naval battle where the Holy League beat the Ottoman fleet.

clue.text: Exact recipes can be varied.

indicators.note: varied means changed around, so the letters rearrange

explanation.surface: Precise recipes can be adapted.
explanation.definitionFit: Precise means exact and accurate.

clue.text: Terror overcame me, having had nightmare

indicators.note: overcame read as came over, covered, so one word wraps round the other

parts.note: dread is great fear or terror

explanation.surface: Fear overwhelmed me after a bad dream.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a fright after a bad dream; the definition is the last three words.
explanation.definitionFit: To have dreamed covers having a nightmare, a frightening dream.

clue.text: In trough, I may appear more shabby

indicators.note: in means the letter is placed inside the other word

parts.note: a manger is a feeding trough

explanation.surface: Placed in a feeding trough, I might look scruffier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' puts I inside MANGER.
explanation.definitionFit: Mangy means scruffy and shabby, so mangier means shabbier.

clue.text: Tom Pearce's horse is nondescript

definitions.meaning: in the English folk song Widecombe Fair, Tom Pearce lends his old mare

explanation.definitionFit: The mare in the folk song Widecombe Fair is grey, and grey also means drab or featureless.

clue.text: Have in hand, working at last on file

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word

parts.note: a rasp is a coarse file

explanation.surface: To keep something in hand, work at last with a file.
explanation.definitionFit: To grasp is to hold firmly, to have it in one's hand.

clue.text: Clamorous about initially defective share of employment

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: vocal means loud and outspoken

indicators.note: the word is missing its first letter, faulty at the start

parts.note: a ration is a share or allowance

explanation.surface: A noisy fuss about a faulty allotment of jobs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially defective' cuts the first letter, leaving ATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Vocational means relating to a job or trade, as in vocational training.

clue.text: Came half up to summit

indicators.note: half up means the first half of the word is turned upside down, read backwards in a down light

explanation.surface: He came halfway up to the peak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half up' reverses only CA, giving AC, and ME stays.
explanation.definitionFit: The acme is the highest point, the peak.

clue.text: German state finally lost for leading Nazi

indicators.note: the word loses its last letter

parts.note: Hesse is a state of Germany

explanation.surface: A German state was eventually lost by a top Nazi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally lost' removes the last E of HESSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudolf Hess was Hitler's deputy in the Nazi party.

clue.text: Are you staying a day in Rome? Most uninteresting

indicators.note: staying read as holding or keeping in, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: thou art is the old form of you are
the ides was a fixed day of the month in the Roman calendar

explanation.surface: A tourist asks whether you are stopping a day in Rome, and finds the answer very dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Are you' is the archaic 'art thou'; the ides was a fixed day in each Roman month.
explanation.definitionFit: Arid means dry and dull, so the superlative is the most boring.

clue.text: Conference fixture

definitions.meaning: a gathering of people for discussion
a sporting event scheduled on a given day, such as a race day

explanation.definitionFit: A meeting is a gathering to confer, and also a sporting fixture such as a race meeting.

clue.text: Removes some clothes and leaves the rest

definitions.meaning: takes off garments, one layer at a time
breaks away from the group, as an aircraft does from a formation

explanation.definitionFit: To peel off is to strip garments and also to veer away from a group or formation.

clue.text: Particularly slowing down in wit

parts.note: esp is the abbreviation for especially, meaning particularly
rit is the musical abbreviation for ritardando, slowing down

explanation.surface: Especially when slowing down in conversation, cleverness shows.
explanation.definitionFit: Esprit is lively wit or spirit, a word borrowed from French.
